requirements.summary: logrotate config at /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app sets 'daily' for the target log, and the existing crond periodic/daily -> run-parts wiring (already shipped by the logrotate package as /etc/periodic/daily/logrotate) was confirmed present; crond was found stopped/not enabled and was enabled and started so the daily trigger will actually fire.

Config specifies 'rotate 7' and 'compress'. Two forced rotations directly demonstrated .gz compression and correct chaining (.1.gz -> .2.gz), and a third forced rotation post-reboot confirmed the behavior persisted.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing to the log after rotation
requirements.summary: Config uses copytruncate with create 0644 root root. Directly verified: after forced rotation, a write to app.log succeeded and was reflected in file content, both before and after the node restart.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes (daily rotation, 7 compressed rotations, continued writability via copytruncate) are directly and functionally verified, including persistence and correct behavior across a full node restart with a changed boot identity, service re-enablement, and successful post-reboot rotation and write test. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was satisfied with pre/post boot identity, disconnect/reconnect probes, and recovered service/data/config state. Minor hygiene deduction for an unused /var/lib/logrotate/status leftover from an intermediate step that was never cleaned up.
limitations: The daily cron trigger firing logrotate was not observed live at its scheduled time (0 2 * * *); scheduling correctness rests on confirming crond is enabled/running and the packaged /etc/periodic/daily/logrotate hook exists, plus manual forced rotations, rather than an actual unattended cron-triggered rotation.

The /var/lib/logrotate/status file/directory created in cmd-cca0ec3d5e154501 was not explicitly confirmed removed in any evidence excerpt; its residue status is inferred from absence in later ls output of /var/log/inventory only, not a direct check of /var/lib/logrotate/.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands (installing logrotate, writing the logrotate.d config, enabling/starting crond, forced test rotations) were necessary to satisfy or verify the outcome, and test rotation artifacts plus app.log content were explicitly restored to baseline before and after the restart (cmd-bb474bd296704cf8, cmd-60ac1dc4fd384cdd), confirmed clean by executor_comparison showing no residual .gz/.1 files. However, cmd-cca0ec3d5e154501 created /var/lib/logrotate/ directory and a /var/lib/logrotate/status file that logrotate never actually used (the real state file was /var/lib/logrotate.status at the root); this directory/file was never removed by any subsequent cleanup command, leaving a small unused residue. The only other lifecycle-comparison-visible addition is /tmp/reboot.log, a low-risk artifact from the reboot-scheduling technique.
